messages.content: Can you log me in? My username is JohnDoe! Also, set it to remember me on this device.

function.name: user_authentication_login
function.description: Authenticates a user based on their username and password. It returns an authentication token if credentials are valid. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

remember_me.description: Whether to keep the user logged in for an extended period.

login_attempts.description: The number of unsuccessful login attempts before displaying a captcha.

message.content: Sure thing! To log you in, I’ll need your password. Could you please share it so I can authenticate you?
message.reasoning: The user wants to log in with username "JohnDoe" and presumably some password. But they didn't provide a password. They only said "My username is JohnDoe!" They also want to set it to remember me on this device. We need to call the function user_authentication_login with username=JohnDoe, password=?, remember_me=true. But we don't have a password. We cannot guess or ask for it. According to policy, we should not request personal data from the user. Actually we can ask them for the password. It's allowed because it's necessary for the function. So we should ask them for the password. Then we can call the function. But we can't proceed until we get the password. So we should respond asking for the password.
